content: I prostrate to all the Victors of the ten directions together with their spiritual heirs.To liberate infinite beings from cyclic existence,I make boundless prayers with a pure and altruistic intention.By the infallible Triple Gem and those of power and might,May these words of truth be fulfilled through the power of the Sages.Throughout all my successive births,May I never be born in the lower realms,The evil destinies, or the states of downfall,But may I obtain a human body endowed with leisure and fortune.From the moment of birth, may I never be attachedTo the pleasures of cyclic existence, but in order to attain liberation,May I engage with unslackening diligenceIn seeking the holy life through the intention of renunciation.When I seek to go forth into the religious life,May neither my retinue, kin, nor wealthCreate any obstacles, and may all favorable conditionsBe fulfilled exactly as I have intended.After going forth, for as long as I live,Just as I pledged in the presence of my preceptor and teacher,May I never be stained by any faults,Whether they be proscribed or naturally unwholesome.Upon the basis of the holy life, may I, through the Great Vehicle,Practice all the profound and vast teachings,And for the sake of all mothers, through many hardships,May I accomplish them for immeasurable eons.May my mind-stream be filled with the many qualities of scripture and realization,With faculties peaceful, well-tamed, and accompanied by a loving heart,Possessing the courage to work for the sake of others without weariness,May I be cared for by a sublime spiritual friend.Just as Sadaprarudita relied upon Dharmodgata,With my body, life, and possessions, unwavering,May I perfectly please the sublime spiritual friend,And never cause them even a moment of displeasure.The meaning of the Perfection of Wisdom, profound, peaceful, and free from elaboration,Untainted by the waters of the stains of wrong views,Just as it was taught to Sadaprarudita,May it always be taught to me in that same way.May I never fall under the power of thoseWho turn away from the intent of the Sage,Who teach the views of eternalism and nihilism,Or of non-virtuous friends and evil companions.Hoisting the great banner of completely pure extraordinary resolve,Propelled by the wind of unremitting diligence,Having well-secured the vessel of hearing, contemplation, and meditation,May I deliver all sentient beings from the ocean of cyclic existence.To the extent that I hear much and give generously,And through the wisdom of pure ethical discipline and discernment,To the extent that my mind-stream becomes superior,May I be free from all forms of arrogance.By the power of pure reasoning, may I discern the meaning of the scripturesExactly as they are, without relying on others;In the presence of the learned, may I engage in the hearingOf the infinite scriptures, with an insatiable thirst.By the four principles of reasoning, may I investigate the meaning of what I have heard,Properly and thoroughly, throughout the day and night;And upon the objects of contemplation, through the wisdom arising from reflection,May I cut through all doubts with an analytical mind.When I gain conviction through the wisdom arising from reflectionRegarding the extremely profound modes of the Dharma,Then, with the diligence that severs attachment to this life,May I rely on solitude and practice as it should be practiced.When, through hearing, reflection, and meditation, the essential pointsOf the Conqueror’s intent are cultivated within my stream of being,May the appearances of this life, which crave for worldly existence,And the mind that seeks its own happiness, never arise.With a mind free of attachment to all the possessions I own,May I overcome all stinginess;And by first gathering sentient beings through material gifts,May I satisfy them with the Dharma.Even the minor trainings I have received,With a mind of renunciation, until enlightenment is attained,May I never forsake, even at the cost of my life,But always uphold the victory banner of liberation.When sentient beings, through malice, strike or disparage me,Whether I see, hear, or recall them to mind,May I be free of anger and, in return,Praise their qualities and practice patience.To attain the virtuous qualities not yet attained,And to cause those already attained to increase ever higher,May I completely abandon the three types of laziness that cause decline,And apply myself to joyful effort.Lacking the power of special insight that suppresses the extreme of existence,And devoid of the moisture of compassion that suppresses the extreme of peace,May I abandon the calm abiding that mostly casts one into cyclic existence,And meditate upon their union.Fearing the profound meaning of the natural state,And grasping as supreme a mind-made, partial emptiness,May I thoroughly abandon all such base, erroneous views,And realize that all phenomena are primordially empty.Pure ethical training is severed by a shameless mind,And one does not fear actions condemned by the holy.May I even lead those monastics of degenerate conduct and false appearance,To establish them in faultless ethical discipline.Abandoning the authentic path, they have entered the base path of error,And have fallen under the power of non-virtuous spiritual friends and evil companions.May I, with ease,Establish all such beings upon the path praised by the Victorious Ones.With the lion’s roar of my exposition, debate, and composition,May I snatch away the confidence of the fox-like pack of erroneous speakers,And by whatever means are suitable to tame them, may I accept them as my own,To uphold the victory banner of the teachings that shall never decline.Wherever I am born, from the moment I drink the nectarOf the speech of the Sage,May I possess high birth, beauty, wealth, and mastery, along with wisdom,And may I be endowed with longevity, freedom from illness, and happiness.Toward those who constantly harbor the intention to harmMy body, my life, and my possessions,And even toward those who speak unpleasant words to me,May I, all the more, cherish them as a mother does her child.Without delay, may I,Generate within my continuum the bodhicitta that cherishes others more than myself,And by cultivating this pure and superior intention,May I bestow the state of unsurpassed enlightenment.May whoever sees, hears, or calls these aspirations to mind,And those who keep them in their thoughts,Be without discouragement in accomplishingThe entirety of the vast prayers of the Bodhisattvas.Through the power of a pure and superior intention,By the force of these vast aspirations I have made,May I fully complete the perfection of aspiration,And fulfill the hopes of all embodied beings.Thus, this aspiration, virtuous in the beginning, middle, and end, Was composed by the widely learned Gyalkhampa Losang Drakpa Pel, At the glorious Zhoto Drigung Thil.
